CONSTRAINTS-B07.title: DEFAULT fills a value
CONSTRAINTS-B07.q: Insert an order without giving a OrderStatus, then check which OrderStatus it got.
CONSTRAINTS-B07.how: OrderStatus has DEFAULT ('Open'), so SQL Server fills it when the INSERT leaves the column out.

CONSTRAINTS-I03.title: ON DELETE CASCADE
CONSTRAINTS-I03.q: Create ecommerce.CustomerContacts with a foreign key to Customers that deletes contacts automatically when the customer is deleted. Test it with a new customer 9999 who has no orders.
CONSTRAINTS-I03.how: ON DELETE CASCADE deletes child rows with the parent. Use it carefully: one delete can remove a lot of data.

CTE-A06.title: Find missing IDs
CTE-A06.q: Interview classic: find missing numbers in an ID column. Copy the order IDs into #Ids, delete IDs 5 and 10 as setup, then find every missing ID between 1 and the highest ID.
CTE-A06.how: Generate every expected number, then anti-join to find those not present. The maximum goes into a variable first, because the recursive part of a CTE cannot contain an aggregate. Everyday Bazaar has over 30,000 orders, more than the default limit of 100 recursion levels, so OPTION (MAXRECURSION 0) removes the limit.

DML-B01.title: Insert one row
DML-B01.q: Add a new customer: ID 2001, name 'Ava Thompson', number EBC-002001, region West.
DML-B01.how: Always list the columns in an INSERT. The query keeps working if columns are added or reordered later. N'...' marks Unicode text for nvarchar columns.

DML-B02.title: Insert several rows
DML-B02.q: Add two customers in one statement: IDs 2101 and 2102, names 'Maya Ross' and 'Owen Hart', numbers EBC-002101 and EBC-002102, both in the West region.
DML-B02.how: One INSERT can add several rows: separate each row's values with a comma.

DML-A08.title: Delete parents and children in order
DML-A08.q: Add a test customer 9999 with two orders (IDs 99101 and 99102). Then delete the customer and everything that depends on them in the right order, and confirm nothing is left.
DML-A08.how: Delete from the bottom of the foreign key chain upward: first the child rows (orders), then the parent (the customer). In the other order the foreign key blocks the delete. Real rows are often referenced by more tables, so list every child table before deleting.

DML-A09.title: Generate test rows with a set
DML-A09.q: Insert 20 test orders for customer 1 in one statement, one per day starting 2025-01-01, with IDs 100001-100020.
DML-A09.sql:
WITH N AS (
    SELECT TOP (20) ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY (SELECT NULL)) AS n
    FROM sys.all_objects
)
INSERT INTO ecommerce.Orders
    (OrderID, CustomerID, OrderReference, SalesChannel, OrderStatus, OrderTotal,
     ItemCount, OrderDate, PlacedAt, RecordedAt, SellerID)
SELECT 100000 + n, 1, CONCAT(N'EB-TEST-', n), 'A', 'Open', 100, 1,
       DATEADD(day, n - 1, CAST('2025-01-01' AS date)),
       DATEADD(day, n - 1, CAST('2025-01-01 09:00' AS datetime2(3))),
       DATEADD(day, n - 1, CAST('2025-01-01 09:01 +00:00' AS datetimeoffset(3))), 1
FROM N;

SELECT COUNT(*) AS TestRows, MIN(OrderDate) AS FirstDate, MAX(OrderDate) AS LastDate
FROM ecommerce.Orders
WHERE OrderID BETWEEN 100001 AND 100020;
DML-A09.how: Generate numbers with ROW_NUMBER over any large table, then build each row from n. One set-based INSERT is much faster than a loop of 20 inserts.

SET_OPERATIONS-A06.title: Gaps between two sets
SET_OPERATIONS-A06.q: Every day in December 2024 had orders, but not every seller sold every day. List the dates in December 2024 on which seller 73 (Lakeview Hub) had no orders, using a recursive calendar and EXCEPT.
SET_OPERATIONS-A06.sql:
WITH Cal AS (
    SELECT CAST('2024-12-01' AS date) AS d
    UNION ALL
    SELECT DATEADD(day, 1, d) FROM Cal WHERE d < '2024-12-31'
)
SELECT d FROM Cal
EXCEPT
SELECT OrderDate FROM ecommerce.Orders WHERE SellerID = 73;
SET_OPERATIONS-A06.how: Every date in the month minus the dates that have data gives the empty dates.

AGGREGATES-I09.title: STRING_AGG: list in one cell
AGGREGATES-I09.q: For each department, list all seller names in one comma-separated cell, sorted by name.
AGGREGATES-I09.sql:
SELECT Department,
       STRING_AGG(SellerName, ', ') WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY SellerName) AS Sellers
FROM ecommerce.Sellers
GROUP BY Department;
AGGREGATES-I09.how: STRING_AGG joins text values from a group with a separator. WITHIN GROUP sets the order of the items.

STRING_FUNCTIONS-I09.title: STRING_AGG
STRING_FUNCTIONS-I09.q: For each of the first 10 customers (CustomerID 1 to 10), list the sellers they bought from in one comma-separated cell, sorted by seller name.
STRING_FUNCTIONS-I09.sql:
SELECT p.CustomerName,
       STRING_AGG(d.SellerName, ', ') WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY d.SellerName) AS Sellers
FROM (SELECT DISTINCT CustomerID, SellerID FROM ecommerce.Orders WHERE CustomerID BETWEEN 1 AND 10) AS dp
JOIN ecommerce.Sellers  AS d ON d.SellerID  = dp.SellerID
JOIN ecommerce.Customers AS p ON p.CustomerID = dp.CustomerID
GROUP BY p.CustomerID, p.CustomerName
ORDER BY p.CustomerName;
STRING_FUNCTIONS-I09.how: STRING_AGG concatenates values in a group. The DISTINCT derived table stops a customer being listed once per order.
